questions.q: How old was Amaziah when he began to reign and how long did he reign?
questions.a: Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he began to reign and he reigned for twenty-nine years.

questions.q: What was the condition of Amaziah’s heart?
questions.a: Amaziah’s heart was not perfectly devoted to Yahweh.

questions.q: Why did Amaziah not kill the children of the servants who had murdered his father, the king?
questions.a: Amaziah did not kill the children of the servants who had murdered his father because the laws in the book of Moses said that the children must not die for the fathers, but that every person must die for his own sin.

questions.q: How did Amaziah add to the 300,000 chosen men from Judah and Benjamin that were registered by their ancestor’s houses?
questions.a: Amaziah hired 100,000 fighting men from Israel to add to the 300,00 chosen men from Judah.

questions.q: Why did the man of God tell the king he should not let the army of Israel go with him?
questions.a: The man of God told the king the army of Israel should not go with him because Yahweh was not with Israel.

questions.q: What did the man of God say would happen even if Amaziah was courageous and strong in battle?
questions.a: The man of God said that God would throw him down before the enemy.

questions.q: How did the man of God answer Amaziah’s question about what to do about the one hundred talents that he had given to the army of Israel?
questions.a: The man of God told Amaziah that Yahweh was able to give him much more than that.

questions.q: Why was the anger of the army from Ephraim kindled against Judah?
questions.a: Their anger was kindled against Judah because Amaziah separated the army and sent them home.

questions.q: What happened to the ten thousand men of Seir when Amaziah led his people out to the Valley of Salt?
questions.a: Amaziah led his people out to the Valley of Salt and he defeated ten thousand men of Seir.

questions.q: What did the army of Judah do to the additional ten thousand men of Seir who they carried away alive?
questions.a: The army of Judah threw the men of Seir down from the top of the cliff.

questions.q: What did the army of Israel do to the cities of Judah from Samaria to Bethhoron?
questions.a: The army of Israel attacked the cities, struck down three thousand of the people and took much plunder.

questions.q: What did Amaziah do with the gods that he brought back from the people of Seir?
questions.a: Amaziah set the gods up to be his own gods, bowed down before them, and burned incense to them.

questions.q: What did the prophet sent by Yahweh ask Amaziah about the gods of the people of Seir?
questions.a: The prophet asked Amaziah why he sought after the gods of a people whose gods did not even save their own people from the hand of Amaziah.

questions.q: What did the prophet say was God’s reason for his decision to destroy Amaziah?
questions.a: The reason God decided to destroy Amaziah was that Amaziah had done this deed and had not listened to the advice of the prophet.

questions.q: What was the message that Amaziah sent to Jehoash, king of Israel?
questions.a: Amaziah sent a message asking Jehoash to come and meet with Amaziah face to face in battle.

questions.q: Why did the messengers of Jehoash tell Amaziah that he should stay at home?
questions.a: The messengers of Jehoash told Amaziah to stay at home because both Amaziah and Judah would fall.

questions.q: Why would God hand over the people of Judah into the hand of their enemies?
questions.a: God would hand them over to their enemies because they had sought advice from the gods of Edom.

questions.q: What was the result when Jehoash, king of Israel, and Amaziah, king of Judah, met each other face to face at Beth Shemesh?
questions.a: The result was that Judah was struck down before Israel and every man fled home.

questions.q: To what place did Jehoash return after he tore down the wall of Jerusalem and took many valuable objects from the temple and palace, along with hostages?
questions.a: Jehoash returned to Samaria after he tore down the wall of Jerusalem and took all the valuables and hostages.

questions.q: For how many years did Amaziah, king of Judah, live after the death of Jehoash, king of Israel?
questions.a: Amaziah lived fifteen years after the death of Jehoash.

questions.q: Where are other matters written concerning Amaziah?
questions.a: Other matters concerning Amaziah are written in The Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.

questions.q: Where was Amaziah buried after he was killed in Lachish?
questions.a: Amaziah was buried with his ancestors in the City of Judah.

questions.q: What was begun against Amaziah after he turned away from following Yahweh?
questions.a: After Amaziah turned away from following Yahweh, a conspiracy was begun against him.

commentary.text: Amaziah worships the idols of Edom.

Verses 1–13 Amaziah was no enemy to religion, but cool and indifferent friend. Many do what is good, but not with a perfect heart. Rashness makes work for repentance. But Amaziah's obedience to the command of God was to his honour. A firm belief of God's all-sufficiency to bear us out in our duty, and to make up all the loss and damage we sustain in his service, will make his yoke very easy, and his burden very light. When we are called to part with any thing for God and our religion, it should satisfy us, that God is able to give us much more than this. Convinced sinners, who have not true faith, always object to self-denying obedience. They are like Amaziah; they say, But what shall we do for the hundred talents? What shall we do if by keeping the sabbath holy we lose so many good customers? What shall we do without this gain? What shall we do if we lose the friendship of the world? Many endeavour to quiet their consciences by the pretence that forbidden practices are necessary. The answer is, as here, The Lord is able to give thee much more than this. He makes up, even in this world, for all that is given up for his sake.

To worship the gods of those whom Amaziah had conquered, who could not help their own worshippers, was the greatest absurdity. If men would consider how unable all those things are to help them, to which they look whenever they forsake God, they would not be such enemies to themselves. The reproof God sent by a prophet was too just to be answered; but he was bidden not to say a word more. The secure sinner rejoices to have silenced his reprovers and monitors; but what comes of it? Those that are deaf to reproof, are ripening for destruction.

Never was a proud prince more thoroughly mortified than Amaziah by Joash king of Israel. A man's pride will bring him low, Pr 29:23; it goes before his destruction, and deservedly brings it on. He that exalteth himself shall be abased. He that goes forth hastily to strive, will not know what he shall do in the end thereof, when his neighbour has put him to shame, Pr 25:8. And what are we when we offer to establish our own righteousness, or presume to justify ourselves before the Most High God, but despicable thistles, that fancy themselves stately cedars? And are not various temptations, is not every corruption, a wild beast of the desert, which will trample on the wretched boaster, and tread his haughty pretensions to the dust? A man's pride shall bring him low; his ruin may be dated from his turning from the Lord.
